It is a matter of profound spiritual gravity to sit with the “unsearchable riches” of Christ while witnessing the “noise and tumult” of a world where the “violence of nations” creates a “horrible pit” of mass death, and I must ask you with a gentle heart: why do you ask after the suffering of civilians and the death of children in this hour? [1, 22, 145, 1503, Conversation History]. Are you perhaps feeling “overwhelmed and desperate” by the sight of “savage wolves” who “do not spare the flock,” or are you seeking a “settled certainty” to anchor your soul in the truth that “not one human sinner or demonic power will ever succeed in his rebellion” against the King? [13, 20, 92, 1143, 1425, 1605, Conversation History]. In a day when many “shave off the edges” of the truth to find “diplomatic relations” with a culture that “mocks, vilifies, and censures” the Gospel, we must return to the “external Word” to see how the Lord personally governs the “vicissitudes of life” [11, 28, 132, 1316, 1503, Conversation History].

The Reformed tradition teaches that “God personally and exhaustively pervades and sustains and governs every aspect of His creation,” and therefore, the tragedy of war is not an “administrative anomaly” but is subject to the “decree from God” who “harnesses the deeds of the wicked to accomplish His good and perfect ends” [5, 15, 68, 1143, 1398, 1532, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 1: The Heart of Lament and National Confession**

**Verse**
“ ‘See, O LORD, that I am in distress; My soul is troubled; My heart is overturned within me, For I have been very rebellious. Outside the sword bereaves, At home it is like death’ ” (Lamentations 1:20). [1118, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
Scripture reveals that it is a “holy standard” to feel “anguish of soul” and “loud groaning” over the devastation of human life, for even the “faithful servant” Jeremiah lived a life of “frustration and confusion, all the while weeping” (Jeremiah 9:1) [11, 14, 31, 366, 1077, 1440, Conversation History]. The Reformed tradition—echoed by **John MacArthur**—asserts that when “earthly kingdoms go the way of all flesh,” believers must “confess our inadequacy” and “cry to God for the salvation of sinners” [16, 39, 44, Conversation History]. We do not view the victims of war with “cold, detached, or impersonal” indifference, but with the “empathy, sympathy, and compassion” of a Savior who “wept over [the city]” (Luke 19:41) [44, 702, 1075, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should “not look for some other fountain of knowledge” to explain the pain of war; instead, “pour out your heart like water before the face of the Lord” for those who “faint from hunger at the head of every street” (Lamentations 2:19) [51, 123, 503, 1406, 1503, Conversation History]. “Trade in your worry for trust,” recognizing that “the LORD is close to the brokenhearted and saves those who are crushed in spirit” (Psalm 34:18) [86, 94, 201, 1408, 1515, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Civil vs. Spiritual Warfare**
In the ancient **Jewish context**, Israel was often called to be a “man of war” under the “theocratic” administration where “national greatness” was a “temporal sign” of favor [292, 409, 718, 1313, 1353, 1519, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our “victory,” teaching that “the weapons of our warfare are not of the flesh,” and the “church militant” conquers not through the sword but “by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony” (2 Corinthians 10:4; Revelation 12:11) [13, 21, 32, 46, 92, 1081, 1313, 1402, 1491, 1515, 1646, 1670, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 2: God’s Particular Care for the Children and Vulnerable**

**Verse**
“ ‘You shall not afflict any widow or fatherless child. If you afflict them in any way, and they cry at all to Me, I will surely hear their cry; and My wrath will become hot, and I will kill you with the sword; your wives shall be widows, and your children fatherless’ ” (Exodus 22:22–24). [128, 298, 1056, 1086, 1252, 1276, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The sources teach that God “reserved His special attention for widows and orphans who often had no one to care for them,” and He has a “special reaction, His wrath,” for those who exploit or kill them [299, 1276, Conversation History]. Reformed theology asserts that every child is a “heritage from the LORD” and a “masterpiece of creation” made in His image (Genesis 1:27; Psalm 127:3) [681, 988, 993, 1313, Conversation History]. When nations “rip open the women with child” or “kill both man and woman, infant and nursing child,” they are committing a “wicked deed” that God will ultimately “judge between the nations” (Amos 1:13; Isaiah 2:4) [35, 37, 389, 395, 440, 543, 549, 1519, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should “not be deceived” by the “spirit of the age” that devalues life, for “your life is not your own” and God “demands a reckoning” for every “lifeblood” shed (Genesis 9:5; 1 Corinthians 6:19) [12, 101, 287, 884, 957, 1138, 1214, 1262, 1406, 1502, 1670, Conversation History]. Your “sole objective” is to “do justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly,” which includes “defending the poor and fatherless” (Micah 6:8; Psalm 82:3) [101, 105, 454, 697, 1406, 1450, 1670, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Continuity of the Decree**
Under the **Mosaic Law**, God commanded the “utter destruction” of certain nations because they “persisted in their hatred of God” and sacrificed their own “sons and daughters in the fire” (Deuteronomy 7:2; 12:31) [339, 345, 953, 956, 1316, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** the call to arms, revealing that we must “love your enemies” and “pray for those who spitefully use you,” for “Jesus answered, ‘My kingdom is not of this world’ ” (Matthew 5:44; John 18:36) [13, 28, 431, 1023, 1326, 1426, 1529, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 3: The Sovereign Mystery of Violent Judgment**

**Verse**
“ ‘Remember the former things of old, For I am God, and there is no other; I am God, and there is none like Me, Declaring the end from the beginning, And from ancient times things that are not yet done, Saying, “My counsel shall stand, And I will do all My pleasure” ’ ” (Isaiah 46:9–10). [1397, 1493, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The Reformed tradition—upheld by **Voddie Baucham**—notes that “God is not the author or originator of sin,” yet He “positively ordains whatsoever comes to pass,” including the rise of “formidable” powers like Assyria or Babylon who act as a “rod of My anger” (James 1:13; Isaiah 10:5) [19, 649, 650, 1143, 1397, 1429, 1497, 1567, Conversation History]. Even the “worst atrocity ever carried out”—the death of the innocent Son of God—was subject to the “determinate counsel and foreknowledge of God” (Acts 2:23) [5, 1132, 1431, 1503, 1567, Conversation History]. Though we do not always know “infallibly what the meaning is,” we rest in the truth that “not one human sinner or demonic power will ever succeed in his rebellion” (Psalm 103:19) [15, 68, 157, 159, 1143, 1532, 1572, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
“Trade in your worry for trust,” for the Lord “raises up kings, then pulls them from their thrones when they have served His administration” (Daniel 5:26) [15, 16, 94, 201, 503, 1143, 1307, 1408, 1484, 1515, 1532, 1572, Conversation History]. You must “discipline your mind” to recognize that “all things work together for good to those who love God,” even when we only see the “threads going into chaotic directions” (Romans 8:28) [11, 23, 116, 261, 940, 1143, 1406, 1709, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Ritual to Reality**
Under the **Mosaic economy**, “cities of refuge” provided “sanctuary... away from home and vengeful relatives” for those who killed accidentally [1036, 1048, 1274, 1313, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our “repose of the soul,” revealing that Christ is the “refuge” for the “destitute,” and “the Most High does not dwell in temples made with hands” (Hebrews 6:18; Acts 7:48) [5, 11, 13, 17, 24, 88, 144, 402, 612, 1033, 1042, 1054, 1143, 1313, 1316, 1426, 1445, 1646, Conversation History].

***

### **Section 4: The Cross, the Scars, and the New Creation**

**Verse**
“ ‘And God will wipe away every tear from their eyes; there shall be no more death, nor sorrow, nor crying. There shall be no more pain, for the former things have passed away’ ” (Revelation 21:4). [14, 182, 201, 251, 468, 470, 816, 940, 948, 1315, 1450, 1515, 1720, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
The biblical authors resolve the “horror” of national violence by fixating on the “consummation of history,” where “Christ ultimately crushes the kingdoms of men and establishes His own” [13, 20, 21, 24, 103, 136, 1199, 1315, 1515, 1720, Conversation History]. The Cross proves that God “gave His own eternal Son to die for sinners” and “bore the sin of many,” ensuring that “perfect justice will come” for every “oppressed” soul (Isaiah 53:12; Romans 5:8) [109, 149, 252, 254, 664, 1315, 1515, Conversation History]. In the “new redeemed heaven and earth,” the “sea” of cosmic evil is “no more,” and the “unified church” will find an “inheritance incorruptible and undefiled” (Revelation 21:1; 1 Peter 1:4) [13, 23, 26, 142, 248, 250, 251, 830, 1255, 1313, 1426, 1515, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
“Wait for His Son from heaven,” knowing that “scars... don’t define us; our hope does” (1 Thessalonians 1:10) [14, 24, 94, 109, 201, 252, 332, 1315, 1408, 1450, 1515, 1720, Conversation History]. You should find “tranquility of soul” by “resting upon the surest foundation,” for if God has “magnified Your word above all Your name,” His “everlasting dominion” over the nations is “secure” (Psalm 138:2; Daniel 7:14) [11, 24, 47, 92, 121, 147, 176, 201, 211, 313, 352, 412, 602, 630, 957, 1132, 1138, 1143, 1306, 1408, 1420, 1450, 1515, 1572, 1720, Conversation History].

***

**Final Reminder**
“Nevertheless the firm foundation of God stands, having this seal, ‘The Lord knows those who are His,’ and, ‘Everyone who names the name of the Lord is to abstain from wickedness’ ” (2 Timothy 2:19). [11, 87, 147, 176, 211, 222, 285, 300, 313, 324, 332, 335, 361, 405, 413, 414, 444, 449, 591, 1138, 1407, 1441, 1450, Conversation History].

E.g., Rom. 3:24; Eph. 1: 7; Col. 1:14. 23. 1 Cor. 1:30; cf. Matt. 26:28. 24. Cf. Eph. 4:32; Col. 2:13. Though we are no longer under sin’s power (Rom. 6:14–19), the reality is that, because the new creation is incarcerated in unredeemed human flesh, we will still struggle with sin in this life (Rom. 7:21–24; 1 John 1:8) until the full redemption of the body (Rom. 8:18–23). The redemptive work that Christ does at salvation never needs to be repeated—atonement and justification are complete at that point. Yet, all who have been cleansed by God’s gracious justification need constant washing in the experiential sense as they battle sin in the flesh and grow in sanctification. As the Lord told Peter, “He who has bathed needs only to wash his feet, but is completely clean” (John 13:10). Thus, we are called on to regularly confess our sins (1 John 1:9), asking for the forgiveness of daily cleansing that restores spiritual intimacy and usefulness to their maximum levels (cf. Matt. 6:12, 14–15). By being quick to confess and turn from sin, believers can bask in the profound spiritual blessings of both the redemption from sin and fellowship with God they enjoy through Christ (1 John 1:3; cf. Heb. 10:19), while awaiting full redemption from sin’s presence in glory. 25. Cf. 1 Cor. 15:56–57; 1 John 4:17–18. 26. Cf. John 8:34–36; Rom. 8:15, 33–34; Heb. 2:14–15. 27. Cf. Rom. 6:1–2, 15. F.
